name: Compliance & Security
one_liner: Enterprise-aware: document management, data protection and security shape the architecture.
purpose: The PM²-Agile model is enterprise-aware and considers the organisation's policies and communications related to information systems. It addresses three aspects — document management, data protection and security — and each of them feeds the Architecture Overview rather than sitting beside it. Data protection defaults to the General Data Protection Regulation, and security is handled through a dedicated practice built around a Security Plan inside a Security Certification Statement.

diagram.sec: What the Security Certification Statement does
items: Tests and evaluates the technical features of the system

fields.what: PM²-Agile considers the organisation's policies and communications related to information systems when addressing compliance and security.
fields.pollux: ESM policy binds the portal even though delivery is agile.

fields.what: When the solution has a document management aspect, regardless of medium, the organisation's defined procedures must be considered.
fields.pollux: Gutenberg (DMO) still has a say in how report packs are retained.

fields.what: PM²-Agile recommends creating a checklist based on the defined procedures to verify whether document management considerations apply.
fields.pollux: Checked when the portal's export and archive behaviour is designed.

fields.what: The checklist should be used when outlining the Architecture Overview, so compliance shapes the architecture.
fields.pollux: Einstein applies it before the Architecture Overview is baselined.

fields.what: Another key aspect of the document management approach is guaranteeing as much interoperability as possible between systems and users.
fields.pollux: Report outputs must be usable outside the portal by national authorities.

fields.what: Guidance on data protection should be defined as part of the software engineering practices and aligned with the specific legislation.
fields.pollux: Brandeis (DPC) shapes the practice, not just a sign-off at the end.

fields.what: By default PM²-Agile focuses on the General Data Protection Regulation, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, on processing personal data of individuals.
fields.pollux: Relevant once national-authority users are granted access in Release 3.

fields.what: When developing a solution, specific data processing requirements must be documented.
fields.pollux: Who sees which member state's data, and on what basis.

fields.what: Addressing data protection requires close collaboration between several roles to ensure the need to process personal data is properly managed.
fields.pollux: Brandeis and Turing work with Einstein, not after him.

fields.what: The Architecture Overview must reflect all these data protection considerations when proposing the high-level architecture strategy.
fields.pollux: Access control appears in the architecture before Release 3 is planned.

fields.what: Because security is critical, PM²-Agile recommends defining a specific practice to address it when building a solution.
fields.pollux: Turing (LISO) is named in the POLLUX cast for exactly this.

fields.what: Documents all security-related activities and lists the actions ensuring the system is developed securely and has appropriate security features.
fields.pollux: Covers both the build environment and the portal's own controls.

fields.what: It defines the security requirements and provides a step-by-step management plan to meet those requirements.
fields.pollux: Requirements land as enabler stories in the Work Items List.

fields.what: An encompassing statement that tests and evaluates technical features, reviews administrative, personnel and physical safeguards, and formally accepts residual risks.
fields.pollux: Signed before national-authority access goes live.

fields.what: Additional elements of the Security Certification Statement are the Security Test Plan and Report and the Security Risk Assessment.
fields.pollux: Produced alongside the team's own Test Plan.

traps: PM²-Agile defaults to the GDPR, Regulation (EU) 2016/679, for data protection.
The document management checklist is used when outlining the Architecture Overview.
The Security Plan sits inside the Security Certification Statement, not beside it.
Residual risks are formally accepted by senior management, not by the team.
Compliance is enterprise-aware — organisation policies bind an agile team too.
